places.summary: Armies from the west coast came in on the wilderness side to reach Ammonihah.

refs.note: The Lamanites came in upon the wilderness side.
They went over to the land of Ammonihah.
Mormon’s army moved to Joshua, by the west seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson infers a mountain pass here. Mormon later held it for fourteen years from Joshua.

places.name: Joshua
places.summary: Joshua was a land in the borders west by the seashore.

refs.note: Joshua was in the borders west by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this was the first named Nephite land on the west coast.

places.name: David
places.summary: David was a land the Nephites lost in their retreat from Zarahemla.

refs.note: The Lamanites drove the Nephites out of the land of David.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows David on the road from Zarahemla to the western pass.

places.name: Angola
places.summary: Angola was a city Mormon’s army fortified and then lost.

refs.note: Mormon’s army took and fortified the city of Angola.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Angola northwest of Zarahemla, near David.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: Judea was a Nephite city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Helaman marched his young men to the city of Judea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Judea west of the Sidon, in the southwest part of the land.

places.name: Cumeni
places.summary: Cumeni was a city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Cumeni was one of the cities the Lamanites had taken.
Helaman’s army besieged the city of Cumeni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Cumeni on the climb toward the western pass.

places.name: Zeezrom
places.summary: Zeezrom was a city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Zeezrom was one of the cities the Lamanites had taken.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Zeezrom between Judea and Antiparah.

places.name: Antiparah
places.summary: Antiparah was a strong Lamanite-held city in the southwest.

refs.note: Antiparah was one of the cities the Lamanites held.
Helaman marched near Antiparah toward a city by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Antiparah at or near the top of a southern pass. The road then fell to the coast.

places.name: Southern pass
places.summary: A road led past Antiparah to a city in the borders by the seashore.

refs.note: The city beyond was in the borders by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson infers a second pass through the western mountains here.

places.name: City by the seashore
places.summary: Helaman named a city beyond Antiparah, in the borders by the seashore.

refs.note: Helaman marched as if going to the city beyond, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places this unnamed city below the southern pass, on the west coast.

places.name: Bountiful
places.summary: Bountiful was the land and city at the north end of the land southward.

refs.note: Bountiful bordered the land called Desolation.
The Lamanites chased Teancum until they came near the city Bountiful.
People gathered at the temple in the land Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places the city near the beach, at about sea level. He estimates it was about 12 miles from Mulek.

places.name: Jershon
places.summary: Jershon was a land by the east sea, south of the land Bountiful.

refs.note: Jershon was on the east by the sea and joined the land Bountiful.
The Lamanites did not dare attack the Nephites in Jershon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson keeps Jershon inland of the coastal road. He says Amalickiah’s drive passed it by.

places.name: Mulek
places.summary: Mulek was a city on the east borders by the seashore.

refs.note: Mulek was among the cities on the east borders by the seashore.
Moroni took the city Mulek.
Nephi and Lehi preached at Mulek.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the people of Zarahemla first settled near here. He puts Mulek about 12 miles from Bountiful.

places.name: Gid
places.summary: Gid was a city in the east borders, near Mulek.

refs.note: Gid was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.
Nephi and Lehi went from Bountiful to Gid.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Gid straight inland from Mulek. Both were the same distance from Bountiful.

places.name: Omner
places.summary: Omner was a city on the east coast.

refs.note: Omner was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Omner was about 20 miles south of Mulek along the shore.

places.name: Morianton
places.summary: Morianton was a city in the east borders, next to the land of Lehi.

refs.note: The people of Morianton disputed land with the people of Lehi.
Morianton was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Morianton a little inland from the beach road.

places.name: Lehi
places.summary: Lehi was a city in the east borders near Morianton.

refs.note: The Nephites built the city of Lehi in the north, by the seashore.
Lehi was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Lehi near the coast, north of Moroni.

places.name: Moroni
places.summary: The city of Moroni stood by the east sea, near the Lamanite border.

refs.note: The city of Moroni was by the east sea, near the Lamanite lands.
Amalickiah began by taking the city of Moroni.
The city of Moroni sank into the depths of the sea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the edge of Nephite land here. It was only about 80 miles from the neck.

places.name: Nephihah
places.summary: Nephihah was a city between the land of Moroni and the land of Aaron.

refs.note: Nephihah lay between the land of Moroni and the land of Aaron.
The text names Nephihah first among the cities taken.
Moroni recaptured the city of Nephihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Nephihah inland from the shore. His map 3 shows Amalickiah passing it by.

places.name: Antionum
places.summary: Antionum was the Zoramite land near the east seashore.

refs.note: Antionum lay east of Zarahemla, nearly bordering the seashore, south of Jershon.
The Lamanites left Antionum to go round about in the wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson calls Antionum the enemy base nearest the narrow neck.

places.name: Siron
places.summary: Siron was a land among the borders of the Lamanites.

refs.note: Corianton went to the land of Siron, among the Lamanite borders.

sorenson.text: Sorenson gives no position for Siron. The map puts it near Antionum only because Alma 39 follows that mission.

places.name: Nephi (Lehi-Nephi)
places.summary: Nephi was the first Nephite city in the promised land. Later it was the Lamanite king’s city.

refs.note: Nephi’s people called the place Nephi.
Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi.
The king of the Lamanites lived in the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates about 22 days of foot travel to Zarahemla. That is about 180 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Shilom
places.summary: Shilom was a land next to Nephi. Zeniff’s people lived there too.

refs.note: Zeniff’s people repaired the walls of Lehi-Nephi and Shilom.
Noah’s tower overlooked Shilom and Shemlon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Shilom was within about ten miles of Nephi.

places.name: Shemlon
places.summary: Shemlon was a Lamanite land below Nephi.

refs.note: Noah’s tower overlooked Shemlon.
Noah looked toward Shemlon and saw a Lamanite army in the borders.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the near edge of Shemlon within about 20 miles of Nephi.

places.name: Place of Mormon
places.summary: Mormon was a place with a fountain of pure water, near the borders of Nephi.

refs.note: Mormon was in the borders of the land.
The place, the waters, and the forest of Mormon are named together.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Mormon was one to three days from the city of Nephi.

places.name: Jerusalem (Lamanite city)
places.summary: This Jerusalem was a city the Lamanites and Amulonites built in the land of Nephi.

refs.note: The city of Jerusalem joined the borders of Mormon.
Waters came up in the place of Jerusalem.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the waters of Mormon were a lake. Jerusalem and Mormon both bordered it.

places.name: Ani-Anti
places.summary: Ani-Anti was a Lamanite village that Aaron visited after Jerusalem.

refs.note: Aaron came over to a village called Ani-Anti.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not place the village. He notes Aaron came over to it from Jerusalem.

places.name: Helam
places.summary: Helam was the land where Alma’s people settled after fleeing King Noah.

refs.note: They fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.
They called the land Helam.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Helam in a mountain valley. He estimates it was no more than 85 miles from Nephi.

places.name: Valley of Alma
places.summary: Alma’s people camped in this valley after one day of travel from Helam.

refs.note: After traveling all day, they called the valley Alma.

sorenson.text: Sorenson counts this day in the 13 days from Helam to Zarahemla.

places.name: Amulon
places.summary: Amulon was a land settled by King Noah’s former priests.

refs.note: The lost Lamanite army found the priests in the land of Amulon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Amulon was not far from Nephi. The rough land still got an army lost.

places.name: Land of Ishmael
places.summary: Ishmael was a Lamanite land where Ammon taught King Lamoni.

refs.note: Ammon went to the land of Ishmael.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Ishmael among lands the Lamanites settled. He does not place it.

places.name: Middoni
places.summary: Middoni was a Lamanite land where Aaron and others were jailed.

refs.note: Ammon’s brethren were in prison in the land of Middoni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Middoni among lands the Lamanites settled. He does not place it.

places.name: Land of first inheritance
places.summary: Lehi’s family first landed here, by the west seashore.

refs.note: They arrived at the promised land.
The place of their fathers’ first inheritance was on the west, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the landing in the far south of the land southward, near sea level.

places.name: Mocum
places.summary: Mocum was a city covered by waters at the time of Christ’s death.

refs.note: Waters came up in the place of the city Mocum.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not know Mocum’s position. His map 15 guesses at it.

places.name: Narrow neck of land
places.summary: A small neck of land joined the land northward and the land southward.

refs.note: A Nephite could cross from sea to sea in a day and a half.
Hagoth launched his ship by the narrow neck.
The Jaredites built a city where the sea divides the land.

sorenson.text: Sorenson argues for 60 to 125 miles across. A narrow neck would not fit Limhi’s lost explorers.

places.name: Narrow pass
places.summary: The narrow pass led by the sea into the land northward.

refs.note: The pass led by the sea into the land northward.
Moroni told Teancum to secure the narrow pass.
Mormon fortified at the narrow pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the pass near the east sea. He thinks large groups could enter the land northward only here.

places.name: Hagoth’s shipyard
places.summary: Hagoth built ships on the borders of Bountiful and launched them into the west sea.

refs.note: Hagoth launched his ship into the west sea, by the narrow neck.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks ships were used because no good land road ran up the west coast.

places.name: Gathering place against the robbers
places.summary: Lachoneus gathered the people into one place between Zarahemla and Bountiful.

refs.note: The people gathered in one body.
They gathered in the land between Zarahemla and Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the area was small enough for the robbers to surround it.

places.name: Desolation
places.summary: Desolation was the land, and later a city, just north of the narrow neck.

refs.note: The land northward was called Desolation.
Mormon gathered his people at the land Desolation.
The Lamanites took the city Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the last Nephite wars stayed near this city. They also reached the hills north of it.

places.name: Teancum
places.summary: Teancum was a city in the borders by the seashore, near Desolation.

refs.note: The city Teancum lay in the borders by the seashore, near Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Teancum northeast of Desolation.

places.name: Boaz
places.summary: Boaz was a city the Nephites fled to after losing Desolation.

refs.note: The Nephites fled to the city of Boaz.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Boaz on the second retreat.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: Jordan was a city the Nephites held during their last retreat.

refs.note: The Nephites held the city of Jordan.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Jordan north of Boaz.

places.name: Jashon
places.summary: Jashon was a land and city near the place where Ammaron hid the records.

refs.note: The Nephites fled until they came to the land of Jashon.
Jashon was near the land where Ammaron hid the records.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Jashon near the hill Shim. It was near Mormon’s home area.

places.name: Shem
places.summary: Shem was a land and city north of Jashon that Mormon fortified.

refs.note: The Nephites were driven north to the land called Shem.
They fortified the city of Shem.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Shem on the first retreat, north of Jashon.

places.name: Hill Shim
places.summary: Shim was a hill in the land of Antum. Ammaron hid the records there.

refs.note: The records were in a hill called Shim, in the land of Antum.
Omer passed by the hill of Shim.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Shim just south of Cumorah. The Nephites reached Shim before Cumorah.

places.name: Hill Cumorah (Ramah)
places.summary: Cumorah was the hill of the last Nephite battle. The Jaredites called it Ramah.

refs.note: The land of Cumorah had many waters, rivers, and fountains.
The Jaredites gathered at the hill Ramah, where Mormon hid records.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Cumorah about 100 miles north of the narrow pass. He sees no great mountain there.

places.name: Ablom
places.summary: Ablom was a place by the seashore where Omer pitched his tent.

refs.note: Omer came over to a place called Ablom, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Ablom by the east sea, past Cumorah.

places.name: Waters of Ripliancum
places.summary: Ripliancum was a large body of water that stopped an army going north.

refs.note: Coriantumr pitched his tents by the waters of Ripliancum.
From there, Shiz’s army fled south to a place called Ogath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the waters came from highland runoff to the west. Ramah was one day south.

places.name: Ogath
places.summary: Ogath was where Shiz camped near the hill Ramah.

refs.note: Shiz pitched his tents in a place called Ogath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not place Ogath. The map puts it between Ripliancum and Ramah.

places.name: Hill Comnor
places.summary: Comnor was a hill near the valley of Shurr in the Jaredite wars.

refs.note: Coriantumr placed his armies by the hill Comnor.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Comnor with the hills near the east sea. He gives no exact place.

places.name: Farthest Nephite retreat
places.summary: Mormon’s people fled north past Jordan before the final battle.

refs.note: The Nephites fled, and some were swept down and destroyed.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 marks this as the farthest retreat north. It stayed near Cumorah.

places.name: Moron
places.summary: Moron was the Jaredite land where the king lived.

refs.note: Corihor came up to the land of Moron, where the king lived.
Moron was near the land the Nephites called Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Moron in the western highlands. He says the Nephites never lived there.

places.name: Jacobugath
places.summary: Jacobugath was the city of the dissenter Jacob. It burned when Christ died.

refs.note: Jacob led his people to the northernmost part of the land.
The Lord burned the city Jacobugath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Jacobugath was farther north than any other known city.

places.name: Moronihah
places.summary: Moronihah was a city covered with earth when Christ died.

refs.note: Earth was carried on the city of Moronihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this city was in the east borders near Jershon.

places.name: Onihah
places.summary: Onihah was a city covered by waters at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Waters came up in the place of the city Onihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Onihah in the land southward by guess.

places.name: Gilgal
places.summary: Gilgal was a city buried in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Gilgal was sunk and buried.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gilgal in the land southward by guess.

places.name: Kishkumen
places.summary: Kishkumen was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city Kishkumen and its people were burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Kishkumen near the neck by guess.

places.name: Laman
places.summary: Laman was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Laman was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Laman in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gad
places.summary: Gad was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Gad was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gad in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gadiandi
places.summary: Gadiandi was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gadiandi was sunk with Gadiomnah, Jacob, and Gimgimno.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gadiandi in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gadiomnah
places.summary: Gadiomnah was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gadiomnah was among the cities sunk in the earth.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gadiomnah in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gimgimno
places.summary: Gimgimno was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gimgimno was among the cities sunk in the earth.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gimgimno in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Josh
places.summary: Josh was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Josh was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Josh in the land northward by guess.

areas.name: Borders by the east sea
match: \b(?:east sea|sea east|east borders by the seashore)\b

routes.title: Lehi’s family reaches the promised land
routes.text: The ship crossed the sea and arrived at the promised land.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the landing was on the west coast, far south. It was the place of first inheritance.

routes.title: Nephi’s people move to the land of Nephi
routes.text: Nephi’s people fled into the wilderness for many days. They called the new place Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates 80 to 100 miles on foot. The straight line was much shorter.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they landed near the neck by the east sea.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks quarrels slowly pushed some of them up the river to Zarahemla.

routes.title: Mosiah leads his people down to Zarahemla
routes.text: Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi and came down into Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the text always says “down” for this direction. Zarahemla was lower than Nephi.

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Zeniff’s people repaired the walls of Lehi-Nephi and Shilom.

routes.title: Ammon’s men search for Zeniff’s people
routes.text: Sixteen men wandered forty days. They did not know the way up.

sorenson.text: Sorenson points to Mosiah 7:4. The searchers knew they had to go up.

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they passed through the neck without knowing it. He estimates about 400 straight-line miles.

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates about 11 miles a day with families and flocks.

routes.title: Alma’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: One day to the valley of Alma, then twelve more days to Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson adds the trips for 22 or 23 days from Nephi to Zarahemla. That is about 250 miles walked.

routes.title: Limhi’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: Limhi’s people went around the land of Shilom toward Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the regular road to Manti went through Gideon.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this shows very broken country. Both lands were within about 85 miles.

routes.title: The Amlicite battles
routes.text: The fight moved from Amnihu to Gideon, then back to the river crossing.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says all this took about 36 hours. So the area spanned only tens of miles.

routes.title: Alma goes over to Gideon
routes.text: Alma went over to the east of the river Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Gideon was about one day from Zarahemla.

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Alma circled the Sidon basin, where most Nephites lived.

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they went up the west coast unseen, then crossed a pass.

routes.title: The sons of Mosiah go up to Nephi
routes.text: They journeyed many days in the wilderness to reach the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the same hard climb as Ammon’s search party.

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Jershon
routes.text: The converted Lamanites left Nephi. The Nephites gave them the land of Jershon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes that travelers went over an upland to reach Jershon.

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Melek
routes.text: The people of Ammon left Jershon and came over into the land of Melek.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Melek was the safest place. Mountains guarded it on the west.

routes.title: Lamanites go “round about” to Manti
routes.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and went round about by the head of Sidon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this took weeks. The east wilderness was too rough to cross directly.

routes.title: Moroni marches to Manti
routes.text: Moroni left part of his army in Jershon and marched to the land of Manti.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes Moroni still had time to ask Alma, get an answer, and march.

routes.title: Morianton flees toward the land northward
routes.text: Morianton’s people fled toward the land northward. They were stopped by the narrow pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Morianton took the road nearer the coast.

routes.title: Teancum heads off Morianton
routes.text: Moroni sent an army to head off Morianton. They met him at the pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Teancum took a different, inland road and got there first.

routes.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
routes.text: Amalickiah took city after city on the east borders by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 3 shows the army staying down by the seashore. The text also lists Nephihah and Gid as taken.

routes.title: Teancum draws the Lamanites out of Mulek
routes.text: The Lamanites chased Teancum down by the seashore until they came near Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Bountiful to Mulek at about 12 miles in a straight line.

routes.title: Moroni retakes the east coast
routes.text: The Lamanites fled from city to city, then down to the seashore and Moroni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this was one day of marching. The southward part was 15 miles at most.

routes.title: Helaman’s young men march to Judea
routes.text: Helaman marched the two thousand young men to the city of Judea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says they came south from their home in Melek.

routes.title: Helaman lures the army out of Antiparah
routes.text: They marched near Antiparah as if going to the city by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the road went past the summit and down to the coast.

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes most settlers went north overland. Two ships are not heard of again.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the main move went overland through the narrow pass.

routes.title: Coriantumr strikes the center
routes.text: A Lamanite army came into the center of the land and took Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson calls this attack a mistake. It played to Nephite strength in the center.

routes.title: Nephites driven into Bountiful
routes.text: The Nephites were driven into the land of Bountiful and fortified a line.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they left by the west pass and fortified the west coast plain.

routes.title: Nephi and Lehi preach from Bountiful
routes.text: They began at Bountiful, then Gid and Mulek, then Zarahemla and Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the east coast held half of the Nephite lands of that time.

routes.title: People gather from the south
routes.text: The people came from all parts of the land into one place.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes people came from the south and from colonies in the north.

routes.title: People gather from the north
routes.text: People in the land northward also came to the gathering place.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this only makes sense for one joined territory north and south.

routes.title: Mormon’s army leaves the land southward
routes.text: The Nephites lost Angola and David. They moved to Joshua, then fled north.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they held the western pass from Joshua for fourteen years.

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the last wars stayed within about 100 miles of the narrow pass.

routes.title: Lamanites cross the neck
routes.text: The Lamanites came down to the city of Desolation to battle.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows the attacks coming north through the neck.

routes.title: Omer flees from Moron
routes.text: Omer passed by the hill Shim and Cumorah to a place called Ablom.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says “many days” suggests a winding route. Moron was near Desolation.

routes.title: The last Jaredite war
routes.text: The war moved east to the hill Comnor, north to Ripliancum, then to Ramah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the last Jaredite battles were in the eastern lowlands. They match the Nephite end.

distances.label: ~180 mi straight · 22–23 days
distances.text: Alma’s people took 8 days, then 13 days. At 11 miles a day, about 250 miles walked.

distances.label: ~75 mi up the river
distances.text: Manti was the farthest settled point upstream.

distances.label: ~160 mi to the Bountiful line
distances.text: About 100 miles downstream, plus two lands of about 30 miles each.

distances.label: ~400 mi straight
distances.text: Limhi’s explorers would not go much past double the expected trip.

distances.label: Day and a half · 60–125 mi
distances.text: The width depends on how far a Nephite went in a day.

distances.label: 2–3 days · ~50 mi
distances.text: “Took his journey over into” suggests more than one day.

distances.label: 3 days · ~50 mi
distances.text: Alma 8:6 gives three days’ journey north.

distances.label: ~1 day
distances.text: The Amlicite story limits these distances.

distances.label: ~12 mi
distances.text: The decoy march and return took one hot day.

distances.label: ~20 mi
distances.text: A guess of about one day’s walk.

distances.label: ~80 mi of Nephite coast
distances.text: Amalickiah had a short road here. The west coast road was over 250 miles.

distances.label: ~200 mi coast to coast
distances.text: Moroni, Nephihah, Aaron, and Ammonihah spread across the land.

distances.label: ≤10 mi
distances.text: Noah could see Shilom from his tower.

distances.label: ≤85 mi straight
distances.text: A lost army found Amulon and Helam.

distances.label: ≤~100 mi
distances.text: The last Nephites did not go much farther north.

figures.title: Overall shape
figures.text: Sorenson begins with Alma 22:32. The land southward is nearly surrounded by water. A small neck joins it to the land northward. The result looks like an hourglass. Both far ends stay unknown.

figures.title: Chief ethnic areas
figures.text: In Alma’s time, Lamanites held Nephi and both coasts. Nephites held the Sidon basin and Bountiful. The Jaredites were already gone. Sorenson says the Nephites sat like a cork in a bottle.

figures.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
figures.text: Amalickiah drove up the east coast toward the narrow neck. Sorenson shows his army staying near the shore. The text names Nephihah and Gid among the cities taken.

figures.title: Teancum intercepts Morianton
figures.text: Morianton fled toward the land northward. Teancum knew he must use the narrow pass. Teancum took another road and got there first.

figures.title: Lamanites go “round about”
figures.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and circled through the wilderness to Manti. The trip took long enough for Moroni to set a trap.

figures.title: Some Jaredite locations
figures.text: Omer went from Moron past Shim and Cumorah to Ablom by the sea. Sorenson links these Jaredite places to the Nephite map. Higher land lay to the west.

figures.title: Limhi’s explorers
figures.text: The explorers missed Zarahemla and kept going north. They found Ether’s plates near Ramah. Sorenson uses this trip to estimate the size of the land.

figures.title: The Amlicite conflict
figures.text: All these moves took place in about 36 hours. So the area around Zarahemla covered only tens of miles.

figures.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
figures.text: Alma taught in Gideon, Melek, Ammonihah, and Sidom. Sorenson thinks he circled the Sidon basin, where most Nephites lived.

figures.title: Four cities across the land southward
figures.text: Moroni, Nephihah, Aaron, and Ammonihah touch one another in the text. Placed side by side, the land is about 200 miles wide.

figures.title: The flight of Alma’s and Limhi’s peoples
figures.text: These two escapes give the best clues to the distance from Nephi to Zarahemla. The online PDF copy is missing this map’s page. The steps here follow Sorenson’s text.

figures.title: Early spread of major groups
figures.text: The early groups stayed small and apart. Sorenson compares them to islands in a sea of wilderness.

figures.title: Expansion in the time of the two Almas
figures.text: By about 50 BC, the Lamanite king ruled from sea to sea. Nephites filled the Sidon basin and moved into Bountiful.

figures.title: Nephite expansion into the land northward
figures.text: Hagoth built a few ships. Sorenson thinks most settlers went north overland through the land Desolation.

figures.title: Possible places of the destroyed cities
figures.text: A few destroyed cities have known places. Sorenson sorts the rest by the order of the list. Many points here are guesses.

figures.title: Final flight from the land southward
figures.text: The Nephites left Zarahemla through Angola and David. They held Joshua by the west sea for years.

figures.title: Final wars in the land northward
figures.text: The last Nephite wars stayed near the narrow neck. They were in the same area as the last Jaredite wars.
